document_title: General Awareness & Reasoning Test - Constitution of Nepal MCQs

questions.question: The existing Constitution of Nepal shall be cited as........

options.d: The Constitution of federal republic Nepal

questions.explanation: Article 1 of the Constitution of Nepal explicitly specifies the short title of the constitution as 'The Constitution of Nepal'.

questions.question: In the constitutional history of Nepal, present constitution is ........... constitution
questions.explanation: Nepal's constitutional evolution includes past constitutions (1948, 1951, 1959, 1962, 1990, and the Interim Constitution 2007), making the 2072 BS Constitution the seventh constitution in Nepal's history.

questions.question: How many parts, articles and schedules are there in the present constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Constitution of Nepal (2072 BS) is structured into 35 parts, 308 articles, and 9 schedules.

questions.question: Constitution of Nepal is amended for the first time on
questions.explanation: The first amendment to the Constitution of Nepal was officially promulgated on Falgun 16, 2072 BS to address inclusive representation and federal delineation concerns.

questions.question: Which of the following isn't the feature of Constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Constitution establishes a democratic, republican, federal, and secular system; 'feudalism' is entirely contradictory to its constitutional framework and democratic values.

questions.question: According to the present constitution of Nepal, Nepal is a;
questions.explanation: Article 4 of the Constitution defines Nepal as an independent, indivisible, sovereign, secular, inclusive, democratic, socialism-oriented, federal democratic republican state.

questions.question: Which provision of the Constitution of Nepal cannot be enforced through Court?
questions.explanation: Directive Principles and Policies of the State serve as guidelines for governance and policy formulation, and they are explicitly non-enforceable by any court of law.

questions.question: Which of the following is not characteristic of constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Civil society is an independent public sphere and community sector, not a structural government organ or institutional characteristic mandated by the Constitution.

questions.question: Which one of the following features is/are support the federal character of Constitution of Nepal?

options.a: Distribution of powers between Centre and States

questions.explanation: Federal systems rely on the constitutional division of power between levels of government, constitutional supremacy, and unified or harmonized legal standards like single citizenship.

questions.question: Which odd one out is as mentioned in right to freedom in constitution of Nepal 2072?

options.a: Freedom to move and reside in any part of Nepal

questions.explanation: 'Freedom to live with dignity' is protected under the separate Right to Live with Dignity (Article 16), whereas options a, c, and d fall under the Right to Freedom (Article 17).

questions.question: Which level of government has the residual power as per the constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: According to Article 58, any power not explicitly enumerated in the federal, provincial, concurrent, or local lists remains with the Federal government as a residual power.

questions.question: Which of the following words is mentioned in the preamble of the constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Preamble of the Constitution of Nepal begins with the opening statement: 'We, the sovereign people of Nepal...'

questions.question: According to Constitution of Nepal, Sovereignty of Nepal is vested on
questions.explanation: Article 3 explicitly declares that the sovereignty and state authority of Nepal are vested in the Nepali people.

questions.question: The final interpreter of Constitution is a
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court holds ultimate judicial authority and serves as the final constitutional interpreter and guardian of the Constitution.

questions.question: How many constitutional organs are there in Nepal?
questions.explanation: Part 21 of the Constitution establishes 13 independent constitutional bodies (such as the CIAA, Auditor General, Public Service Commission, Election Commission, etc.).

questions.question: Which of the following is not the basic element of the national interest of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Article 5 defines national interest to include independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity, nationality, and economic well-being; geographical diversity is a physical characteristic rather than a national interest element.

questions.question: The Constitution of Nepal mentioned national language is as
questions.explanation: Article 6 states that all mother tongues spoken as the mother tongues in Nepal are the national languages of the nation.

questions.question: All languages spoken as the ...... in Nepal are the languages of the nation.
questions.explanation: The constitutional provision recognizes all mother tongues spoken across Nepal as languages of the nation.

questions.question: The term 'secular' has been used in the Present Constitution in
questions.explanation: Article 4 ('Definition of State') defines Nepal as a secular ('dharmanirpeksha') state.

questions.question: In which article of Constitution of Nepal has provisioned about National interest?
questions.explanation: Article 5 of the Constitution outlines provisions regarding the protection and promotion of Nepal's national interest.

questions.question: How many types of Citizenship have been provisioned by the Constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Constitution provisions 4 types of citizenship: descent (Banshaj), naturalized (Angikrit), honorary (Sammanak), and non-resident Nepali (NRN) citizenship.

questions.question: There is the provision of citizenship in the ...... of constitution of Nepal.
questions.explanation: Part II (Articles 10 through 15) of the Constitution contains all legal provisions governing citizenship.

questions.question: According to Constitution of Nepal, provision of citizenship with identity of .....
questions.explanation: Citizenship provisions account for lineage through descent as well as gender identity considerations (such as obtaining citizenship through either mother's or father's identity).

questions.question: In which constitution of Nepal, the fundamental rights of citizens were included?
questions.explanation: The Government of Nepal Act, 2004 BS was the earliest constitutional instrument to introduce foundational rights provisions in Nepal's history.

questions.question: In which constitution of Nepal, the fundamental duties of citizens were included?
questions.explanation: The Constitution of Nepal of 2019 BS first introduced explicit clauses regarding the fundamental duties of citizens.

questions.question: How many fundamental rights are there under present Constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Part 3 of the Constitution (Articles 16 to 46) guarantees a total of 31 fundamental rights to citizens.

questions.question: In the Present constitution of Nepal, the rights to freedom and rights to property are respectively mentioned in the articles and ...
questions.explanation: Article 17 deals with the Right to Freedom, and Article 25 covers the Right to Property.

questions.question: In which Article of the constitution of Nepal, the rights to communication is mentioned?
questions.explanation: Article 19 of the Constitution explicitly guarantees the Right to Communication, protecting freedom of the press and publication.

questions.question: Which articles of the present Constitution of Nepal is related with Abolition of Untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 24 guarantees the Right against Untouchability and Caste-based Discrimination.

questions.question: Right to open political parties' is ...
questions.explanation: The freedom to form and operate political parties, associations, and unions is a constituent clause under the Right to Freedom (Article 17).

questions.question: Right against trafficking, slavery or servitude according to Constitution of Nepal is ...
questions.explanation: Article 29 guarantees the Right against Exploitation, prohibiting human trafficking, slavery, forced labor, and servitude.

questions.question: Who is not entitled for social security rights as per the constitution of Nepal?

options.b: tribes on the verge of extinction

questions.explanation: Article 43 covers social security for indigent, incapacitated, and helpless citizens, single women, persons with disabilities, and endangered tribes, whereas general minorities have specific cultural/linguistic protections rather than indigent social security entitlements.

questions.question: Rights to Information, is lies under the ... of the constitution of Nepal.

options.a: A rights to receive secret matters

questions.explanation: The Right to Information is enshrined as Article 27 under Part 3 (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution.

questions.question: In the context of fundamental right, present constitution of Nepal has guaranteed free education for the Nepalese ...
questions.explanation: Article 31 specifies that every citizen has the right to access free education up to the secondary level from the State.

questions.question: "No law shall be made providing for the death penalty to any one", which article deals with this statement?
questions.explanation: Article 16 (Right to live with dignity) explicitly establishes that no law shall be enacted providing for the death penalty.

questions.question: Which article provides a citizen of Nepal, shall not discriminate against anyone on the basis of religion, caste, Sex?
questions.explanation: Article 18 guarantees the Right to Equality, ensuring equal protection of law and prohibiting discrimination based on origin, religion, race, caste, or sex.

questions.question: Which of the following right is guaranteed as fundamental right for the first time by the Constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Right of Senior Citizens (Article 41) was introduced as a standalone fundamental right for the first time in the 2072 Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following subject does not lie under political right?

options.d: Rights to security of personal prestige

questions.explanation: Security of personal prestige and dignity relates to individual human and personal rights rather than political rights such as voting or running for public office.

questions.question: "No law shall be made providing for the death penalty of any one." According to the Constitution Nepal, this related to
questions.explanation: The abolition of capital punishment is anchored directly within the Right to live with dignity under Article 16.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct in regards in right to freedom provisioned in the constitution of Nepal?

options.c: Freedom to assemble peaceably and without arms

questions.explanation: Article 17(2)(b) precisely guarantees the freedom to assemble peaceably and without arms.

questions.question: The right, which is first time guaranteed in the constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Right of Victims of Crime (Article 21) is a new fundamental right introduced in the 2072 Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following right(s) is/are guaranteed as fundamental right for the first time by the constitution of Nepal, 2072?
questions.explanation: Consumer rights, right to housing, and dalit rights were all newly or more comprehensively secured as explicit fundamental rights in the 2072 Constitution.

questions.question: According to the constitution of Nepal, which provision among the given below does not fall under fundamental rights?
questions.explanation: While children, women, and senior citizens have separate fundamental right provisions, 'Rights of Youth' is not designated as an independent fundamental right article.

questions.question: Which is not fundamental right under Constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Proselytizing or inducing religious conversions is restricted by law; a 'right to conversion of religion' is not a fundamental right.

questions.question: "Every woman shall have right relating to safe motherhood and reproductive health", which article deals with this statement?
questions.explanation: Article 38 covers the Rights of Women, which includes specific guarantees for safe motherhood and reproductive health.

questions.question: Rights to Social Justice is related to with
questions.explanation: The Right to Social Justice (Article 42) is built upon the inclusive principle, ensuring proportional participation of marginalized groups in state structures.

questions.question: According to Article 47 of the Constitution of Nepal, within how many years, should the legal provisions be made for the implementation of fundamental rights
questions.explanation: Article 47 mandates that the State must enact necessary legal provisions within three years of the commencement of the Constitution to enforce fundamental rights.

questions.question: Which is/are the duties of Citizens according to the Constitution of Nepal

options.a: To render compulsory service as and when the state so requires
options.b: To protect and preserve public property
options.c: To abide by the constitution and law

questions.explanation: Article 48 sets forth all these clauses as the constitutional duties of every citizen.

questions.question: The existing Constitution of Nepal has incorporated duties of Citizens in
questions.explanation: Citizen duties are explicitly incorporated under Article 48 of the Constitution.

questions.question: Fundamental Rights in Nepal are guaranteed by it through
questions.explanation: Article 46 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, serving as the legal shield that guarantees the enforcement of all fundamental rights.

questions.question: How many duties of citizen's have been provisioned by the Constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Article 48 outlines 4 distinct duties for citizens of Nepal.

questions.question: According to Constitution of Nepal, every citizen shall have ...

options.b: Freedom of assemble peacefully without arms
options.c: Freedom to move and reside any part of Nepal

questions.explanation: All listed individual liberties are guaranteed under the clauses of Article 17 (Right to Freedom).

questions.question: According to Constitution of Nepal, which is not the duty of the citizens?

options.a: To abide by the Constitution and law
options.b: To render compulsory service as and when the state so requires
options.c: To protect the political rights of the people.
options.d: To protect and preserve public property

questions.explanation: Protecting the political rights of people is not among the formal constitutional citizen duties listed in Article 48.

questions.question: In which constitution of Nepal, the directive principles were included?
questions.explanation: The Interim Constitution of Nepal, 2007 BS, first introduced the inclusion of directive principles of state policy.

questions.question: How many directive principles have been provisioned by the present constitution of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Article 50 outlines 4 core Directive Principles of the State (political, social/cultural, economic, and international relations).

questions.question: In which articles of the constitution of Nepal, has guaranteed about the "Public Service"?
questions.explanation: Policies relating to basic needs, governance, and public service delivery are outlined under Article 51 of the Constitution.
Statement I is true because directive principles are non-enforceable guidelines; Statement II is true because Article 41 establishes the Right of Senior Citizens.

questions.question: Which of the following are listed as a directive Principle of State Policy?

options.a: Policies relating to national unity and national security
options.b: Policies relating to political and governance system of State
options.c: Policies relating to social and cultural transformation

questions.explanation: State policies under Article 51 cover national unity/security, political governance, and social/cultural transformation.

questions.question: Match the following and choose the correct answer.
questions.explanation: Article 56 corresponds to Structure of state (a-1), Article 58 corresponds to Residual Power (b-4), Article 60 governs Distribution of sources of revenue (c-2), and Article 61 establishes the President (d-3), yielding the matching combination a1, b4, c2, d3.

questions.question: How does the constitution of Nepal define the state power?

options.a: The responsibility issuing general directives, controlling and regulating of the governance of Nepal is the state power
options.b: The power relating to the executive, Legislature, Judiciary and residual power is the state power
options.c: The power relating to the executive, Legislature, Judiciary of the state is the state power

questions.explanation: State power in Nepal encompasses executive, legislative, judicial, and residual powers as constitutional competencies.

questions.question: Which article of Constitution of Nepal provides for the federal structure of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Article 56 details the structure of the State, establishing Nepal's federal model comprising the Federation, Province, and Local levels.

questions.question: How many schedules of the constitution of Nepal have listed the power of state distributed to federation, province and local level?
questions.explanation: Schedules 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 outline the federal list, provincial list, concurrent lists, and local list, totaling 5 schedules.

questions.question: In which Schedule the Constitution of Nepal has provisioned about National Flag of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Schedule 1 contains the shape, geometric construction method, and description of the National Flag of Nepal.

questions.question: In constitution of Nepal, the list of local level power is provided in ...
questions.explanation: Schedule 8 contains the list of exclusive legislative powers of local governments (municipalities and rural municipalities).

questions.question: Eighth Schedules of the constitution relating to ... contain ... items
questions.explanation: Schedule 8 details the exclusive powers of local governments, consisting of 22 specific items.

questions.question: According to the Constitution of Nepal which amongst the following is the authority of a province?
questions.explanation: Trust management (Guthi) falls under provincial jurisdiction (Schedule 6), whereas central statistics, health policies, and intellectual property are federal or concurrent matters.

questions.question:
Which of the following pair(s) is/are correctly matched?
1. Seventh schedule - concurrent powers of Federation, Province and local level
2. Fifth schedule - Federal list
3. Sixth Schedule - Province List
4. Ninth Schedule - ...
questions.explanation: All listed schedules match their respective legislative competency categories accurately within the constitutional schedule framework.

questions.question: How many Policies of the State have been provisioned in the article 51 of the Constitution of Nepal promulgated in 2072 BS?
questions.explanation: Article 51 of the Constitution enumerates 13 distinct policies under the Directive Principles and Policies of the State.

questions.question: How many members of the Constituent Assembly signed the Constitution of Nepal when it was promulgated?
questions.explanation: Out of the 601 total members of the Constituent Assembly, 507 members signed the final document during its promulgation in 2072 BS.
